sanskrit_verse:
अवस्करस्थलश्वभ्र भ्रमस्यन्दनिकादिभिः
चतुष्पथसुरस्थान रथ्यामार्गान् न रोधयेत्
transliteration: avaskarasthalaśvabhra bhramasyandanikādibhiḥ | catuṣpathasurasthāna rathyāmārgān na rodhayet
sph_interpretive_translation: One must not obstruct pathways designated for communal movement by dumping refuse, excavating pits, causing obstructions, or creating barriers at crossroads, sacred sites, streets, or highways.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the maintenance of collective access and mobility
Causation arises from deliberate acts that impede natural flow and social function
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's ability to control spatial usage
Restoration logic requires removal of obstruction and reinstatement of unimpeded passage
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of shared space as a sacred continuum
executable_legal_axioms: IF any individual or entity places material or immaterial impediments on public pathways THEN automatic obligation to remove such impediments within 24 hours
IF obstruction causes measurable disruption to collective movement THEN responsible party assumes duty to restore functionality without compensation claim
IF repeated violations occur THEN capacity to use public domain is temporarily suspended until alignment with dharma is demonstrated
IF obstruction involves sacred or central junctions THEN restoration includes ceremonial clearing aligned with Vedic protocol
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, obstruction of public ways constitutes violation of fundamental dharmic duty. The threshold of responsibility is established through direct causality and capacity to prevent or cease interference. Authority lies in immediate injunction and mandatory restoration without punitive damages.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes clear causality between act of blocking and disruption of movement. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential impact on individuals and society. Proportional responsibility is tied to extent of obstruction and intent. Non-punitive reality rule upholds that correction restores balance rather than inflicts penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Obligation to personally clear all impediments within prescribed time
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Public acknowledgment of error and commitment to alignment
Capacity Restoration: Reinstatement of right to use public space upon successful demonstration of non-repetition
Integrity Reintegration: Ceremonial cleansing if obstruction involved sacred or central junctions
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law. Dharma is restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the supreme adjudicator.
